raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
When a request contains an assistant message with empty or whitespace-only content (and no tool_calls), the chat template produces a malformed prompt that can cause garbled model output.

Add a validation check in _validate_request that rejects such messages with a 400 error before they reach the model. Assistant messages carrying tool_calls are exempt since null content is expected in that case.

Tests cover:
- Empty string content is rejected
- Whitespace-only content is rejected
- Tool_calls with null content passes
- Non-empty content passes

## Code Review

This pull request adds validation to reject assistant messages with empty or whitespace-only content unless they contain tool calls, along with corresponding unit tests. The review feedback correctly points out that assistant messages with `None` or empty list `[]` content (without tool calls) can still bypass this check and cause issues during template processing. It is recommended to update the validation logic and the unit tests to reject these cases as well.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

If an assistant message has `content` set to `None` (or an empty list `[]`) and does not contain any `tool_calls`, it will bypass this validation check because `isinstance(content, str)` is `False`. However, during template processing (e.g., in `_apply_jinja_template` or the DeepSeek encoders), `None` content is normalized to an empty string `""`. This means `None` content without tool calls will still result in a malformed prompt and garbled output.

We should update the check to reject `None` content and empty lists when no tool calls are present.
